newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen lifeless, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen lifeless, rangebound.

text.p: Argentine stocks were seen flat in muted trading Friday during the U.S. Independence Day holiday, dealers said.
"It's a day we could've skipped," said Adolfo Adorno at Agra traders. "Many people won't even turn up and prices will probably tick sideways."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.9 percent Thursday to set a new five-year high of 831.44 on the back of a rally on Wall Street.
But traders said the bolsa was running out of steam and players would remain cautious.
"We had very good news with the U.S. jobs report Thursday but even if the Dow charges higher, the MerVal will need some more time to consolidate," another dealer said.
He said stocks in the steel and construction sectors remained good buys, while bank, telephone and oil stocks might face a mild correction.

Analysts said long-term prospects remained good based on strong economic growth and corporate mergers involving foreign firms, especially in the banking sector. "But I would advise clients to hold their positions for now," Adorno said.
